_comment: How parsed ingredient names are normalized for ingredient-based recipe matching (see testing/one_off/ingredient_frequency.py). Normalization only removes what doesn't change WHICH ingredient it is. Never add anything here that would merge real varieties (salted vs unsalted butter, light vs dark brown sugar, dutch-process vs natural cocoa). All words are lowercase.
_leading_words: Stripped from the FRONT of a name only, repeatedly, never leaving it empty. Size, state, prep, and unit/container words a parser left behind ('4 ounces (113g) chocolate' leaves 'ounces chocolate'). Words that change the ingredient ('ground' ginger, 'toasted' sesame oil, 'whole' milk, 'dried' apricot) don't belong here.
_leading_phrases: Regular expressions removed from the front of a name before leading_words. Mostly leftovers from lines a parser only half understood: ranges ('7 to 14 g / 1 to 2 tablespoons cornstarch' leaves 'to 14 g / ...'), a second measure, 'plus a pinch of'.
_equivalents: Whole normalized names that mean the same ingredient, written differently. Applied last, after plurals are removed.
_ignore: Normalized names left out entirely: placeholders nobody would list as something they have.
_plural_exceptions: Plurals the simple suffix rules would get wrong.
